speaker: The Chairman
text: Supplementary Estimates of Expenditure for the financial year 1 April 2018 to 31 March 2019, contained in Paper Cmd 20 of 2019.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I shall deal first with the Head of Expenditure in respect of which an amendment stands on the Order Paper Supplement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I commend the generosity of Singaporeans in donating to our AUs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And I thank the Ministry for providing 1.5 times the matching grant for the three older universities, and three times the matching grant for the three newer universities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: However, I am concerned about how the Ministry budgets for these matching grants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: While our universities receive many donations from alumni and the public, donations are typically small.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The gift of a major donor is several orders of magnitude larger than the average donation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, one big donation can be many times the value of total annual donations in a typical year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, the required matching grants from the Government will also range widely.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I am glad that the Minister for Finance discussed, when closing the Budget Debate, how the Government works hard to ensure forecasts of revenue and expenditures are accurate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: First, could the Ministry of Education (MOE) outline how it budgets for the typical year-to-year variation in donation receipts by our AUs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, what is the planning process to manage the impact of a big grant on the Ministry’s budget?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We have not had a billion-dollar donation to universities yet in Singapore, but I hope we will soon.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: That would make a big impact to the Government's Budget.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, MOE works closely with the AUs to estimate the annual amount of matching grants required.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also plan and budget for long-term horizons, similar to what we do for other lumpy expenditures, such as infrastructure spending.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Where appropriate or necessary, we also spread out the Ministry's matching over a number of years.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: And I thank again the Ministry for continuing to support the AUs in Singapore.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I shall now deal with the remaining Heads of Expenditure in respect of which no amendment stands on the Order Paper Supplement.

speaker: The Chairman
text: In respect of the Main Estimates, they are Heads E, G, O, P, Q, S, T, V, W and X.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I propose to take those Heads of Expenditure en bloc.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will now take the Supplementary Development Estimates.

speaker: The Chairman
text: In respect of the Supplementary Development Estimates, they are Heads E, O, S and X.
